summary: Defensively avoid duplicate local resource pending-trigger inserts.

replay.detail: Resource observation and canonical graph replay semantics do not change. The existing pending queue is flushed at open; this change does not retry previously invalid replica records.

schema.detail: One-time replacement of four persisted local trigger schema objects and a local version marker occurs in one opening transaction. No table or index definition, graph digest, rule, signature, or nonce code changes. Each trigger checks the subject primary key before insertion. The resource observation version remains 2, so existing stores do not rebuild all resource observations solely for this trigger change.

rules.detail: Claim validation, authority, signatures, nonce, checkpoint and replica admission rules are unchanged.

compatibility.detail: Old binaries ignore the extra local marker and use the new trigger SQL, which uses ordinary SQLite SELECT and NOT EXISTS. An old binary reopening the store does not replace those triggers because its definitions use IF NOT EXISTS. A future upgrade checks the marker again. Downgrade behavior has not been executed.

downtime.detail: The first open after upgrade acquires a writer transaction for four DROP/CREATE trigger pairs and metadata, then performs the usual pending flush. The one-time DDL and flush cost are unmeasured; no full resource-observation rebuild is requested by this marker.

manual.detail: No manual migration or configuration change is required for trigger installation. Previously invalid records are not reset or repaired.

recovery.detail: A failed opening transaction rolls back trigger replacement and marker together. In a controlled old-trigger fixture, the first replica-record INSERT and resource-claim INSERT/DELETE succeeded, while re-upserting the same replica record with its subject pending raised the pending-subject UNIQUE error. The NOT EXISTS trigger writes avoid that reproduced conflict. The original invalid records' cause and onset remain unknown. Exact-ID recovery of those records needs a separately reviewed bounded envelope retry path; this change provides no repair command or automatic retry.
